title: A serial worker you can close

blocks.text: The page's table of implementations: `Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor()` has a single thread and guarantees sequential, first-in first-out execution. Since Java 19 an `ExecutorService` is also `AutoCloseable`, so try-with-resources shuts it down and waits for its tasks. And the page asks you to name your threads with a `ThreadFactory`.

items: `new SerialWorker(name)` starts nothing yet; its one thread is a daemon named exactly `name`;
`Future<T> submit(Callable<T> task)` queues a task; tasks run one at a time, in submission order, on that one thread;
`close()` accepts no more tasks (a later `submit` throws `RejectedExecutionException`), and returns only once every task already submitted has run, however long that takes.

rows: five tasks, the first slow, each noting its number and thread
a slow task and a queued one, then `close()`

cases.says: A submitted task runs, and its Future gives the task's result.
All tasks run one at a time on a single thread, in the order they were submitted, even while one of them is slow.
close() waits while tasks are pending and lets the queued ones run instead of dropping them.
The worker's thread carries the name it was given and is a daemon.
Building a SerialWorker starts no thread; its one thread appears with the first task.
After close(), submit throws RejectedExecutionException: a closed worker accepts no more tasks.
close() waits for a task that takes 1.5 s, however long it runs, rather than giving up after a timeout.

concepts: Since Java 19 an ExecutorService is AutoCloseable, and close() shuts it down and waits for its tasks.
newSingleThreadExecutor() runs its tasks one at a time, in submission order, on one thread.
